University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski”
University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski” is a leading higher education institution in the Republic of Bulgaria. As the largest university in Southern Bulgaria and the second largest in the country, it plays a significant role in Bulgaria’s academic landscape. Established in 1961 as the Higher Institute of Pedagogy for Natural Sciences and Mathematics, it was officially granted university status in 1972.
The institution educates more than 13,200 full-time students and approximately 5,000 part-time students across 128 bachelor’s and 110 master’s programs. These programs span various disciplines, including natural sciences, humanities, social sciences, engineering, and economics, and are organized within the following nine faculties:
· Faculty of Biology
· Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics, and Information Technology
· Faculty of Economics and Social Sciences
· Faculty of Pedagogy
· Faculty of Physics and Technology
· Faculty of Philology
· Faculty of History and Philosophy
· Faculty of Chemistry
· Faculty of Law
The University maintains two branches in the towns of Smolyan and Kardzhali.
The University ofPlovdiv “Paisii Hilendarski” is equipped with a library, its own publishing house, an information center, scientific laboratories, language and multimedia laboratories, a distance-learning center, a career-guidance service, a research and development division, a sports center, a student theatre, and other technical and service units.
Support for Scientific Research and Project Implementation at Plovdiv University
Plovdiv University “Paisii Hilendarski” is dedicated to fostering scientific research and innovation through a diverse portfolio of research projects. Each year, the university administers numerous research contracts, supported by key national and institutional funding bodies, including the Bulgarian National Research Fund and the Scientific Research Fund at Plovdiv University. In addition to securing public research grants, the University actively collaborates with industry partners through commercial agreements, facilitating knowledge transfer between academia and the private sector. These funding sources support the advancement of scientific inquiry, the development of innovative solutions, and the promotion of knowledge transfer, reinforcing the University’s role as a leading research institution.
Furthermore, the university actively participates in European Union research and education funding programs, including Erasmus+, Horizon Europe, Interreg NEXT, and various other international funding initiatives. These programs play a crucial role in expanding research opportunities, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and strengthening global academic networks. The University secures funding both independently and through strategic partnerships with higher education institutions across Europe. By engaging in these initiatives, the University enhances its research capacity, facilitates knowledge exchange, and contributes to addressing both global and regional challenges through interdisciplinary and cross-border cooperation.

The Scientific Association for Mechanical Engineering (GTE) is Hungary’s prominent professional and scientific organisation uniting the engineering-intellectual community in the field of mechanical and processing industry. Founded in 1949 as an independent association and tracing its roots back to earlier engineer-associations from the 19th century, it has evolved into one of the largest technical and social organisations in Hungary with more than a thousand individual and corporate members across 27 divisions and all regions of the country. 
GTE’s mission emphasises reinforcing technical competency, facilitating collaboration among academia, research institutions and industry, and promoting the industrial transformation of manufacturing. Its public-benefit goals include supporting research and development, enhancing the added value of domestic mechanical and processing industries, disseminating advanced manufacturing technologies, supporting SMEs, organising training and publishing professional journals. 
GTE has been placing strong emphasis on supporting the digital and sustainable transformation of the Hungarian manufacturing sector. The Association is founding member of national “Industry 4.0” technology platform, helping to facilitate cooperation between university research groups, SMEs and large enterprises. Its programmes increasingly address topics such as additive manufacturing (3D printing), data-driven production, artificial intelligence in manufacturing, and smart factory logistics 
Moreover, GTE is striving to elevate Hungary’s mechanical industrial competitiveness by acting as a conduit for internationally leading technologies and standards. It brings together domestic engineering intellectuals and foreign partners via its membership in international bodies such as the International Academy for Production Engineering (CIRP) and the Fédération Internationale des Sociétés d’Ingénieurs des Techniques de l’Automobile (FISITA). Its current development roadmap also places emphasis on supporting SMEs in integrating advanced manufacturing technologies, promoting industrial standardisation, and publishing research results that facilitate the transition to higher value-added production.

The Aragon Aerospace, Space and Defence Cluster (AERA) is the regional industrial cluster representing the aerospace, space and defence sectors in Aragón (Spain). Established in 2007, AERA brings together more than 60 members, including large companies, SMEs, technology centres, universities and public institutions. Its mission is to foster innovation, competitiveness and collaboration within the regional and European aerospace and defence ecosystem.

Through its participation in European networks and projects, AERA contributes to the development of resilient and sustainable industrial value chains, promotes training and skills development, and supports the dual-use application of technologies for both civil and defence markets. The recently established spin-off company, OPMET Labs s.r.o., focuses on developing innovative technologies and measuring devices in the field of optical metrology, primarily aimed at measuring the shape of optical surfaces and wavefronts of optical systems. These devices are intended for use in the manufacture of optical elements or complex systems designed for applications in space, high-power lasers, and sensitive diagnostic instruments. In addition, they are expected to find broad application in the production of consumer electronics and other industries.
The measuring devices employ several innovative approaches and unconventional principles, including absolute interferometry based on tunable lasers, generation of optical twins of the simulated system, utilization of graphic multicore units, and the application of selected machine learning principles.
The company’s team builds upon and further develops the expertise transferred from the TOPTEC research centre (Institute of Plasma Physics of the Czech Academy of Sciences). The core group of the company has been intensively dedicated to developing metrological methods and instrumentation for more than 12 years.

The Reiner Lemoine Institute is an independent non-profit research institution that contributes to a transformation towards a sustainable energy supply based on 100 % renewable energy since its founding in 2010. In our many years of experience we have conducted applied research to scientifically support the long-term transition of the energy supply system towards renewable energy. Open source models developed here have firmly established themselves in energy system modeling. Our mobility and electrification concepts have been implemented by private companies as well as the public sector worldwide.

Our scientific research is conducted in three interconnected research units:
Theresearch unit Transformation of Energy Systemsdevelops, investigates, and optimizes future scenarios for a sustainable energy supply. For this, self-developed open source tools are mostly used. Among others these include dialogue and visualization tools for the energy transition
Theresearch unit Mobility with Renewable Energyconducts research at the interface between sustainable drive systems and renewable power generation. As a contribution to the energy transition in the transport sector, we examine how alternatives to gasoline and diesel engines can be incorporated in renewable energy systems in an economically and ecologically reasonable manner and what charging infrastructure will be needed in the future.
Theresearch unit Off-Grid Systemsdevelops electrification strategies based on renewable energy for developing regions and optimizes hybrid mini-grids with the help of simulation models and geographic information software. By this we especially support the UN Sustainable Development Goal for affordable and clean energy (SDG7) as well as climate action (SDG13).

Sogetel S.r.l. is an Italian company operating in the ICT sector since 1981, with its legal and operational headquarters in Rome. The company provides high-tech services and solutions, supporting its clients in their digital transformation journey. It specializes in data management, processing, and valorization, customized software development, complex systems design, and the implementation of innovative solutions in fields such as Big Data, Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things (IoT), and Cybersecurity.
Sogetel’s revenues come from three main business lines:
- Specialized ICT Consulting: Sogetel offers its clients highly skilled technical-managerial professionals, thanks to a continuous talent scouting and acquisition process.
- Turnkey Software Development: Design, development, and maintenance of custom software applications for clients.
- Proprietary Innovative Solutions: The company has a dedicated department for the design and development of proprietary products and innovative solutions, based on market research insights and client/prospect feedback (e.g., Isaac, Higitus, Zencluster, KaiSafe, Kainet).
Over the last five years, the company has recorded an average annual turnover of around €8 million, totaling over €22 million in the 2022–2024 period. As of December 31, 2024, shareholders’ equity amounted to €2.49 million.
Across all business lines, Sogetel maintains strong quality control, supported by ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 certifications, and by the constant involvement of technical and commercial managers throughout the entire service lifecycle, ensuring alignment between client expectations and delivered results.
Sogetel has long-standing collaborations with key players in the ICT and industrial sectors, including:
- Main clients: TIM, Vodafone, Fastweb, Engineering, DXC Technology, Capgemini, IBI (pharmaceutical), Octo Telematics, ALD Automotive, Latteria Soresina.
- Strategic and technology partners: Red Hat, Noovle (TIM Group), Confluent, Mare Consulting, Alleantia, Crico Italia.
Thanks to this solid ecosystem of relationships, Sogetel is able to deliver end-to-end solutions, integrating ICT know-how with hardware, sensors, and strategic consulting.
- Proprietary platforms:
- Kainet – Industrial IoT platform
- Isaac DE – Big Data management (NoSQL)
- Isaac TS – Time-series sensor data analytics
- Higitus – AI-based automation and data classification
- Zencluster – Distributed cloud environment for real-time applications
